content.title: 'Stop Nick Shirley Act' raises concerns about free speech, limiting journalism
content.text: A California bill nicknamed the “Stop Nick Shirley Act” by Republicans raises concerns about free speech and journalism. “California is trying to pass a bill that would criminalize investigative journalism with misdemeanors, $10,000 fines, imprisonment, and content takedown,” YouTuber Nick Shirley wrote on the social media platform, X. “The proposed bill is titled AB 2624 and was made after I exposed mass fraud by immigrant groups in America.” Shirley went viral last year for filming a YouTube video where he went around to multiple daycare centers in Minnesota that appeared vacant and alleged there was fraud. Shirley said that under the bill, he wouldn’t be able to do his independent investigations. “Under AB 2624, government-funded entities like the Somali “Learing” Daycare centers would be protected from being exposed if they operated inside California,” he wrote on X. The legislation is titled AB 2624 and was introduced by Assemblywoman Mia Bonta, who argued that the bill would increase confidentiality protections for those who offer immigration support. Assemblyman David Tangipa argued that the bill was unconstitutional because it bans open public video taping of organizations. Bonta pushed back, saying there were no provisions related to journalism of fraud.
